note: Annual election of one third (five seats), Friday 15 January 1915, for the places of H. G. MacGeagh, D.L., John Mahaffy, J.P., Thomas L. Cole, George McGhee and Maxwell Thompson (who did not seek re-election); six candidates, one more than the seats, so that (as the Lurgan Mail of 9 January 1915 put it) a walk-over was averted by one candidate. "Out of an electorate of 2,435 some 1,313 had exercised" the franchise, more than 800 in the last three hours, many of them soldiers of the Ulster Division given leave to vote; "There were only three spoiled votes." George McGhee (Nationalist in 1912) lost his seat. No party labels printed. John Mahaffy: no party label printed in 1915. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Lurgan, Armagh County Council, 28 May 1914, listed as Unionist: Portadown News, 2 May 1914, p. 5 ("Local Government Elections: Armagh County Council"); Newry Reporter, 28 April 1914, p. 5 ("Armagh County Council: Nominations"); Lurgan Area, Armagh County Council, 5 June 1920, printed 'U.': Lurgan Mail, 12 June 1920, p. 6 ("The Elections: County Council"); labels from the Frontier Sentinel, 12 June 1920, p. 5). Henry G. MacGeagh: no party label printed in 1915. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Lurgan, 15 January 1912, printed 'U.': Lurgan Mail, 20 January 1912, p. 5 ("The Municipal Election: A Heavy Poll"); labels from the Lurgan Times, 20 January 1912, p. 2 ("Monday's Election"); Lurgan, 15 January 1923, listed as Unionist: Lurgan Mail, 6 January 1923, p. 5 (advertisement "Lurgan Municipal Election, January 1923": the fifteen candidates adopted by the Joint Committee of the Orange Institution and other local Unionist organisations); Lurgan Mail, 13 January 1923, p. 5 ("Notes and Notions": "the unchallenged return of fifteen Unionist candidates")).
